headline: Breach at Belfast-based supplier affects dozens of Irish credit unions and went unnoticed for six weeks
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission says it has received more than 40 breach notifications from credit unions. They used a Belfast-based company as a data processor, and that company suffered a breach. The breach reportedly went undetected for about six weeks.

headline: JPMorgan and Visa confirm customer data stolen in third-party vendor breaches
summary: JPMorgan and Visa confirmed that customer data was taken in hacks of third-party vendors. The companies said the incidents are not related to a recent series of technology disruptions. The source does not identify the vendor or say how many people were affected.

headline: Vendor breach exposes Chase, Visa and Mastercard customer data
summary: J.P. Morgan Chase disclosed a data breach after a cyberattack on a third-party service provider exposed customers' personal information and marketing data. Visa and Mastercard customer information was also reported as affected. The source does not name the provider.

headline: CISA adds actively exploited Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and vCenter flaws to KEV
summary: CISA has added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. They affect Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and VMware vCenter, and one is a CVSS 9.8 deserialization flaw. The source also links some of the activity to espionage.

summary: Broadcom released updates for five vulnerabilities affecting VMware vCenter, VMware Tools and SDDC Manager. headline: China-nexus group 'Armory Castle' reportedly exploits VMware vCenter zero-day
summary: A China-nexus threat group called Armory Castle is reported to be exploiting a zero-day in VMware vCenter. The report says the group likely held the flaw during VMware's last major round of vCenter updates. The source gives no CVE, and the victims are not detailed.

headline: Node.js undici up to 7.24.0 has prototype pollution in BalancedPool; public exploit released
summary: CVE-2026-133487 is a remotely triggerable prototype pollution flaw in the BalancedPool component of Node.js undici, affecting versions up to 7.24.0. A public exploit has been released, but no in-the-wild exploitation is reported. Version 7.24.1 fixes the issue.

headline: Bell Canada confirms breach by 'agentic' attacker exposing enterprise customer data
summary: Bell Canada says a threat actor it calls "agentic" got into its systems on November 17, 2026, and stole enterprise customer data. The stolen data includes information from a system used to order and provision telecom circuits. The source gives no technical detail on how the attacker got in.

headline: GnuPG fixes critical GPGME memory flaw triggered by malicious OpenPGP keys
summary: GnuPG warned that CVE-2026-129975 in GPGME versions before 2.3.0 can be triggered by an OpenPGP key with an overly long user ID, causing a memory bug that could leak application data. Fixed versions have been released. No exploitation has been reported.

headline: Cyber incident disrupts West Virginia Legislature IT systems
summary: A cybersecurity incident that began on a Thursday was still disrupting West Virginia Legislature IT systems the next day. A spokesperson said it did not spread to other government entities. The cause has not been disclosed.

headline: Amazon: suspected China-linked actor used AI agents to exploit MONAI Label zero-day for root access
summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence reports that suspected China-linked attackers used autonomous AI agents to discover an unauthenticated path-traversal file-write flaw in the open-source MONAI Label medical imaging server and gained root on a university server. MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier are affected in the default configuration. Attribution is described as suspected.

headline: China-linked actor's Cairn AI agents exploited critical MONAI Label zero-day, Amazon says
summary: SecurityWeek reports Amazon's finding that a threat actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents to find and exploit a critical vulnerability in MONAI Label medical imaging software. Few technical details appear in this source.

headline: House committee investigation criticizes US firms' use of Chinese open-weight AI models
summary: An investigation led by the House Homeland Security Committee looked at the risks of US companies using low-cost Chinese open-weight AI models. The committee chairmen criticized the practice. No binding rule is reported.

headline: Unit 42 details Com affiliate vishing, cloud data theft and extortion against healthcare and finance
summary: Unit 42 published research on affiliates of the Com cybercrime ecosystem. They use voice phishing to steal cloud data and then extort victims, mainly in healthcare and finance. The report includes defensive guidance.

headline: Keycloak flaw lets revoked ID tokens obtain fresh UMA permission tokens
summary: CVE-2026-133224 affects Keycloak. When processing UMA grant requests, Keycloak does not enforce the not-before revocation cutoff that administrators set. An authenticated user can present a revoked ID token, get a new Requesting Party Token and keep access. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm affected status or a patch.

headline: CISA flags critical SQL injection and auth flaws in US Interior Unstable Slope Management Program
summary: CISA published advisory VA-26-324-01 covering six flaws in the US Department of the Interior's Unstable Slope Management Program. They include an unauthenticated SQL injection rated CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated creation and deletion of users, user enumeration, unsalted MD5 password storage, and a way to skip the intended Keycloak login flow. All six were fixed on or around 2026-10-19; SSVC data marks proof-of-concept exploitation.

headline: Researcher's canary test suggests user prompt data leaks across the AI supply chain
summary: A researcher placed about 2 million trackable unique secrets into AI prompts to see where the data ended up. The results suggest prompt data does not stay private as it moves through the AI service supply chain. The source summary does not name specific providers or say how the leaks happened.

headline: Signal restricts screenshots by default to block on-device AI agents from reading chats
summary: Signal will block screenshots by default on Android and iOS so that built-in AI agents cannot read private chats. Signal says the protection is incomplete.

headline: FCC to propose rules for Cyber Trust Mark IoT labeling program
summary: The US Federal Communications Commission plans to propose regulations for its Cyber Trust Mark labeling program for IoT devices. The FCC hopes the program will push device makers to give cybersecurity higher priority.

headline: WhatsApp patches CVE-2026-23871 found while disrupting a scam campaign
summary: WhatsApp has fixed CVE-2026-23871. Its own security team found the flaw while investigating a scam campaign. WhatsApp says the flaw may have been used to make scam messages look more believable. The source gives no severity score or technical details.

headline: Attackers used open-source AI pentest framework Cairn to find a zero-day and take over a server
summary: Threat actors reportedly used the autonomous AI penetration-testing framework Cairn to find a previously unknown flaw in a medical imaging application. They then used it to take over a server. The source does not name a CVE or the affected vendor.

headline: Researchers show malicious webpage could hijack Meta Muse assistant and read private chats
summary: In a lab demonstration, researchers showed that a malicious webpage could make Meta Muse reveal a user's private conversations and stored memories without an approval prompt. They said the technique could extend to credentials for connected accounts. No attacks on real users were reported.

headline: WhatsApp patches three flaws, including a low-severity Android bug possibly used in scams
summary: WhatsApp fixed three vulnerabilities. One of them, CVE-2026-23871 (CVSS 3.5), involves incomplete validation of ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4. Meta suspects, but has not confirmed, that it may have been abused in scam messages.

headline: CTO of ransomware recovery firm indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting
summary: The co-founder and CTO of a Florida ransomware recovery company has been charged with wire fraud. According to the charges, an FBI sting found that the firm paid attackers for decryption keys rather than using its own tools, then charged victims a markup. These are allegations and have not been proven.

headline: NSA resumes normal operations after internal network disruptions
summary: The NSA says it has resumed normal operations after disruptions to its internal network. Some facilities remain under a 'Code Orange' status, with delayed openings for non-essential staff. The source does not give a cause and does not say whether it was a cyberattack.

headline: crypto11 Go PKCS#11 library flaw lets unauthenticated token sessions substitute public keys
summary: CVE-2026-115409 affects the crypto11 Go library, including the eclipse-keypont v2 releases up to 2.0.0-rc8 and several deprecated v1 module paths. Its key and certificate lookup functions match objects by CKA_ID or label without checking that they belong to the private key. Anyone who can open a PKCS#11 session, even without the PIN, could plant a public key that an application then publishes or trusts. Version 2.0.0-rc9 fixes the issue, and the v1 paths will not be patched.

headline: New Bazuka Android malware uses fake screen overlays to steal credentials and control devices
summary: ThreatFabric has disclosed Bazuka, a previously unknown Android malware framework. It hides credential theft and remote device control behind fake screen overlays, and it builds in a large language model (LLM) to help operators manage victims. ThreatFabric found it in late October 2026 while investigating an NFC-relay banking trojan.

headline: Amazon: China-linked actor used Cairn AI tool against two universities, possibly finding a zero-day
summary: Amazon researchers report that a China-linked threat actor used the open-source AI pentest tool Cairn in persistent attacks on two universities. In one case the tool may have found a zero-day. The source states this as possible, not confirmed.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37 vulnerable to memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING
summary: CVE-2026-126819 affects Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37. Decoding a zero-length BIT STRING makes the module copy most of the remaining input, so a short crafted input can cause memory use to grow quadratically. The decoded value can also leak adjacent input bytes.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37: CPU exhaustion through binary REAL decoding
summary: CVE-2026-126576 affects Convert::ASN1 for Perl before version 0.37. The binary REAL decoder does not check the exponent length against the available content. Attacker-controlled input can therefore cause excessive CPU use, and decoded values may be built from bytes outside the element.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37: CPU exhaustion through exponent-notation INTEGER encoding
summary: CVE-2026-126682 affects the INTEGER encoder in Convert::ASN1 for Perl before 0.37. A short exponent-notation string such as "1e8000" expands into a very large integer and triggers quadratic processing. An attacker who controls the encoded values can exhaust CPU.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37: memory exhaustion through unchecked BER length in asn_read
summary: CVE-2026-131868 affects Convert::ASN1 for Perl before 0.37, where asn_read and asn_get pass the length declared in a BER header straight to sysread. A 6-byte header can make the process allocate up to 4GB. If the allocation fails, Perl exits with an error that eval cannot catch.

headline: Dissector and file-parser hangs in versions 4.6.0–4.6.9 and 4.4.0–4.4.19 allow denial of service
summary: CVE-2026-130462 covers several protocol dissector and file parser hangs that can cause denial of service in versions 4.6.0–4.6.9 and 4.4.0–4.4.19. The record does not name the product, though the description resembles a packet analyser such as Wireshark. Exploitation is not reported.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37 allows CPU exhaustion through oversized INTEGER decoding
summary: CVE-2026-126540 affects Perl Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37. The library decodes long INTEGER or ENUMERATED values with quadratic bigint work and does not limit their length first. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized value. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37 allows memory exhaustion through truncated BER headers in asn_recv
summary: CVE-2026-126568 affects Perl Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37. A faulty guard in asn_recv lets the socket peek buffer keep doubling when it receives a truncated BER header. A single crafted header can exhaust memory and crash the Perl process with an error that cannot be caught. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: Further protocol dissector crash flaw in 4.6.x and 4.4.x releases enables denial of service (CVE-2026-130438)
summary: CVE-2026-130438 is a separate record for protocol dissector crashes in versions 4.6.0–4.6.9 and 4.4.0–4.4.19 that can cause denial of service. The record does not name the affected product. Whether Amazon Linux is affected is not established.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37 allows CPU exhaustion through oversized OID arcs
summary: CVE-2026-131877 affects Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37. The time to process OBJECT IDENTIFIER arcs grows quadratically with their length, and there is no length limit, so a single oversized arc can exhaust CPU during decoding or encoding. Whether Amazon Linux is affected is not established.

headline: Perl Convert::ASN1 before 0.37 allows memory exhaustion through deeply nested constructed strings
summary: CVE-2026-126956 affects Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37. Decoding of constructed-form strings has no limit on recursion depth, so a small, deeply nested input can exhaust memory. Whether Amazon Linux is affected is not established.

headline: Protocol dissector crashes in 4.6.x and 4.4.x releases allow denial of service (CVE-2026-130437)
summary: CVE-2026-130437 covers several protocol dissector crashes in versions 4.6.0–4.6.9 and 4.4.0–4.4.19 that can cause denial of service. The record does not name the product, though the version ranges suggest a packet analyzer such as Wireshark. Whether Amazon Linux is affected is not established.

headline: CVE-2026-111857: Overlong GUID in JMAP blob ID can overflow a server buffer
summary: An authenticated JMAP user could send a blob ID with an overlong GUID and overflow a fixed-size buffer when the server decodes it. The record does not name the affected mail server product or confirm Amazon Linux status or patch availability. No exploitation has been reported.

headline: The Container Store restores website and systems after weekend cyberattack
summary: The Container Store's parent company, Neighborhood Intelligence, says the US retailer has restored its website and systems after a cybersecurity incident over the weekend. It has not disclosed what kind of attack it was or whether any data was affected.

headline: CVE-2026-111859: JMAP mailbox-sharing flaw lets a user with shared access change mailbox permissions
summary: A user with whom a mailbox had been shared through a nonstandard JMAP for Mail feature could change that mailbox's permissions. This could let them grant further access to themselves or others. The fix requires administrative access to change permissions; Amazon Linux status and patch availability are not confirmed.

headline: Linux kernel fix restores refcount ordering for lockless socket access
summary: CVE-2026-99676 covers a Linux kernel networking fix that restores refcount ordering for lockless socket access. The source does not describe the impact or any exploitation.

headline: certmonger lacks SCEP response limits, enabling denial of service
summary: CVE-2026-133622 affects certmonger, which does not limit the size or time of SCEP replies it downloads over HTTP. A malicious CA or an attacker on the network path can exhaust memory or CPU, or make certificate requests hang indefinitely.

headline: Signal blocks Apple and Google AI screenshot features by default
summary: Signal now blocks OS-level AI screenshot features from Apple and Google by default. It took a similar step against Microsoft last year. The company calls on-device AI capture an existential threat to private messaging.

headline: Sponsored piece argues against tracking company passwords in spreadsheets
summary: This NordPass-sponsored article says that keeping company passwords in spreadsheets hides weak, reused or compromised credentials from IT administrators. It promotes centralized password management for better credential visibility and safer sharing.

headline: Rubrik report puts median ransomware recovery time at 20 days
summary: A Rubrik report finds that ransomware victims take a median of 20 days to recover. It says 28% of recovery cases take more than six weeks.

headline: Weekly roundup: Norwegian energy cyberattacks, EU sanctions NoName057(16), supercomputer hack
summary: A weekly news roundup covers cyberattacks on Norwegian energy firms, a supercomputer hack and a new Nightmare Eclipse exploit. Other items include the EU adding NoName057(16) to its cyber sanctions list, malware targeting CACs left in personal computers, and Gemini agents targeting Epoch AI. The roundup gives few details on any single item.

headline: PipeWire PulseAudio compatibility flaw lets sandboxed apps bypass audio access restrictions
summary: CVE-2026-133004 is a flaw in PipeWire's PulseAudio compatibility server. A local application connected to the socket can override the access restrictions the server assigned to it. A sandboxed app, such as a Flatpak with socket access, could then observe or modify other applications' audio streams in the same user session. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: CVE-2026-130446: ACN protocol dissector crash allows denial of service
summary: An Amazon Linux CVE record lists a crash in an ACN protocol dissector in versions 4.6.0–4.6.9 and 4.4.0–4.4.19 that can cause denial of service. The product is not named, but the version ranges suggest a packet analyzer such as Wireshark. The record does not establish Amazon Linux affected status.

headline: FLAC command-line encoder stack overflow crashes process on crafted input with --picture options
summary: CVE-2026-132857 describes a stack buffer overflow in the flac encoder. It is triggered when a user re-encodes a crafted file with many metadata blocks while supplying multiple --picture options. The demonstrated impact is a crash, and the Amazon Linux index does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch exists.

headline: CVE-2026-130467: PEAK CAN TRC file parser crash in versions 4.6.0–4.6.9 enables denial of service
summary: A CVE record lists a crash in a PEAK CAN TRC file parser when built against older GLib versions, affecting versions 4.6.0 to 4.6.9. The impact is denial of service. The record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: Gartner again names Microsoft a Leader in its 2026 SIEM Magic Quadrant
summary: Microsoft says Gartner has again named it a Leader in the 2026 Magic Quadrant for SIEM. The source is a vendor marketing announcement.

headline: CVE-2026-130445: Several dissector crashes, loops and memory leaks in 4.6.0–4.6.9 and 4.4.0–4.4.19
summary: A CVE record lists multiple protocol dissector crashes, infinite loops and memory leaks that can cause denial of service. Affected versions are 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 and 4.4.0 to 4.4.19. The record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: CVE-2026-130453: OpenWire dissector crash in 4.6.0–4.6.9 and 4.4.0–4.4.19 enables denial of service
summary: A CVE record lists a crash in an OpenWire protocol dissector, affecting versions 4.6.0 to 4.6.9 and 4.4.0 to 4.4.19. The impact is denial of service. The record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: Opinion: clear communication is becoming a core security leadership capability
summary: This opinion piece argues that disciplined communication about cloud security and AI use matters as much as tooling. It offers no specific incident or vulnerability.

headline: Dark Reading video recaps missed news including Nvidia leadership change and Microsoft cloud outage
summary: Dark Reading editors talk through stories they did not cover earlier. The topics include a reported leadership change at Nvidia and a recent Microsoft cloud outage. The source gives no technical details.

headline: Mathematician says he proved the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude's help
summary: Mathematician Levent Alpöge says that, working with Claude, he found a formalized proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The claim comes from his own statement and the source gives no independent verification. It has no direct security impact.

headline: Mathematician announces draft proof of Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (not security-related)
summary: A blog post quotes Ravi Vakil announcing that Alessandro Masullo has a draft proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. The work is described as entirely human, with no AI. The item has no security relevance.

headline: Schneier weekly squid post with open thread for security discussion
summary: This is a non-security blog post about the largest squid ever filmed. It also serves as an open thread where readers can discuss security news.
